Founded in 2019 by members rooted in bluegrass, country, and psychedelic rock, the music is a hard driving mixture of twangy guitar and psychedelic noise, held together by a steady rhythm section with the cry of pedal steel layered in between it all. Electric Tumbleweed has maintained steady momentum in the Northern California music scene; backing David Nelson (New Riders of the Purple Sage) on multiple occasions; most notably at the Mystic Theater with guest Mark Karan (Ratdog) for a sold out performance. Electric Tumbleweed performed regularly at Phil Lesh’s Terrapin Crossroads as a solo group as well as with Scott Law, Barry Sless (Phil Lesh and Friends) and Dave Zirbel (Sammy Hagar Band) are regular pedal steel players in the group. The band has been invited to play multiple festivals and events including The String Cheese Incident’s Hog Farm Hideaway, Ain’t Necessarily Dead Fest (backing David Nelson). We aim to keep our goals high, and to perform high quality music; focusing on writing and arranging new songs, and booking future tour dates. We are excited to release our debut full-length album in October 2021, which features Sam Bush (New Grass Revival), Barry Sless (Phil Lesh & Friends), and Lester and Dylan Chambers (The Chambers Brothers). The album features the artwork of Stanley Mouse/Jennae Bennett and was engineered and mastered by Grammy winning Oz Fritz (Tom Waits).
source: Occidental Center for the Arts, Creative Sonoma

title: Grant-Lee Phillips & Grant Lee Buffalo & Damon Wyckoff
description:
“I’m drawing on the urgency of the moment,” reflects Grant-Lee Phillips. “The things that eat away in the late hours…”

That urgency inspired the headlong rush of his new album Widdershins – in which Grant-Lee Phillips invests the insight, nuance, and wit that has distinguished his songcraft over the past three decades. 

Exploring folk, alternative, pop and Americana, Phillips’ band Grant Lee Buffalo was a seminal ‘90s mainstay. Even in the wake of disbanding in ’99, albums like Fuzzy and Mighty Joe Moon remain enigmatic treasures, that new generations are drawn to. So much so, that Grant Lee Buffalo embarked on a string of reunion dates in 2011. The group signed a deal with Chrysalis/Blue Rain Coat in 2018 and a major reissue of the catalogue is currently underway.

As for Phillips, his career has constantly evolved, diving into deeper adventurous waters with each project. Being a songwriter and a multi-instrumentalist, he’s embraced the freedom of being his own producer. “For me, production is about honoring and delivering the song, baring witness to the spirit in the room. It is so much about communication, finding that common language among musicians and technicians - which is often wordless, by the way.” Fans have come to accept that Phillips would always prioritize creative discovery, while resisting the expected. 

Something he could never expect occurred in 2001 when Phillips was approached about a role on a newly burgeoning TV show called The Gilmore Girls. “The Town Troubadour was sort of a cartoon version of myself. I had no idea it was going to snowball into multiple seasons, coffee mugs and syndication as it did. The show turned a lot of new people onto my music.”

Acting wouldn’t curb Phillips’ consistent output however. Mobilize, Virginia Creeper, Nineteeneighties, Strangelet and Little Moon would follow – each a document of his life in that moment.

On his 2012 release Walking in the Green Corn he drew from his Native American heritage. A year later Phillips relocated from Los Angeles to Nashville, marking a new creative chapter, inspiring The Narrows. The release of Widdershins in 2018 brings the current count to nine solo albums and four with Grant Lee Buffalo.

His eyes remain fixed on the work at hand and that of tomorrow. His tour schedule finds him circling the globe many times over in a given year. Constant movement, physically and creatively is almost a mantra. Say’s Phillips, “I could never sit still.“

title: Monica Da Silva & Complicated Animals
description:
Monica da Silva grew up living between The United States and Belém, Brazil, a city on the Amazon River. A love of travel and foreign language helped to forge her unique sound. 

 

Paralleling her life, da Silva's music contains an eclectic mix of Brazilian and American influences. Her sound can be classified as International Fusion, as it is heavily influenced by Brazilian music, namely Bossa Nova, but also incorporates elements of Lounge, Electronica, Indie Pop, and Worldbeat. Da Silva brings her cultural diversity to her songs, smoothly flowing between English, Portuguese, and Spanish.

 

In 2010, da Silva released her album "Brasilissima" . The record featured songs in both of her native languages - English and Portuguese. The first single "Aí Então", “was chosen by Putumayo World Music to be included on their compilation “Brazilian Beat”. The upbeat, psychedelic track "That's Not The Way" was chosen by the music director of ESPN to be played during the programming of The FIFA World Cup in 2014, alongside major recording artists Coldplay, Sérgio Mendes, Pitbull, Jennifer Lopez, The Black Eyed Peas, Stan Getz, and Astrud Gilberto. 

Da Silva's single "Soldado de Amor" \(2017\) has been featured in the BBC One series "The Replacement”, in the Paramount Network series "American Woman", and in a 2019 campaign for the designer Tory Burch.

Her music has also been featured in the series "Heartland", and in an ad for Patron Tequila. She is currently recording a new, full-length solo album, as well as writing and recording with her project, Complicated Animals.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Holistic Horse Training in Heart and Mind Equine
description:
Bring your horse or learn with the Heart & Mind Equine herd in this hands-on exploration of communication, connection, and kind leadership.

Offered by Heart & Mind Equine Rescue. Meet our rescued therapy horses, explore our volunteer program, and learn about holistic horse keeping and equine-assisted services \(e.g., therapy, coaching, leadership, and team building with horses\). No experience is necessary. All are welcome, including both horse and mental health professionals.

A Different Approach to Horse Training

What happens when we stop thinking about horse training simply as getting a horse to do what we want and start learning to communicate in a language horses naturally understand?

Join us for a 90-minute experiential introduction to Holistic Horse Training with lifelong horsewoman and equine-assisted learning facilitator Alane Freund.

Horses naturally communicate through movement, energy, boundaries, responsiveness, and connection. Their herd relationships include both leadership and following, with every member playing an important role.

Alane describes these dynamics as ranking and linking: leadership in service of relationship, paired with the connection that makes relationship possible.

Holistic Horse Training uses this deeper understanding of herd dynamics to help us communicate with horses through leadership that is clear, kind, respectful, and connected.

What You’ll Learn

Alane will draw from natural horsemanship, TTouch, equine behavior and herd dynamics, and her own Holistic Horse Training exercises to explore:

Reading equine communication and body language

Clear, kind boundaries

Leadership without force

Building trust and connection

Practical training tools and techniques

What horses can teach us about effective leadership in our own lives

Bring Your Horse or Learn With the Herd

Have a horse you’d like to work with? Bring them along.

No horse? No problem. You can participate with members of the Heart & Mind Equine herd.

Come ready to learn, experiment, ask questions, and discover a more connected way of working with horses.

description:
The program leaders will guide you on 8 weekly hikes with the challenge increasing each week. Leaders will have group discussions about gear, hydration, hiking poles, first aid and pacing, etc. The group's final hike aims for Bald Mountain, where hikers can enjoy stunning vistas.

The following is a list of possible routes specifically selected for this hiking series: 

1) Sat 9/26 — Creekside + Waterfall loop, 3.6 miles, 750 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 2) Sat 10/03 – Vista Trail loop, 3.4 miles, 830 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 3) Sat 10/10 – Hillside to Neptune table + Meadow, 4.4 miles, 970 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 4) Sat 10/17 – Goodspeed to Nattkemper bench, 3.8 miles, 1,240 ft elevation \[meet @ Goodspeed lot\] 5) Sat 10/24 – Hillside + Vista Trail loop, 3.6 miles, 1,070 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 6) Sat 10/31 – False Lake Meadow & Lake Ilsanjo loop in Trionne-Annadel SP, 6.1 miles, 670 ft elevation \[meet @ Annadel's Cobblestone Trailhead\] 7) Sat 11/07 – Fern Lake + Orchard loop in SDC/Jack London SHP, 5.5 miles, 1,460 ft elevation \[meet @ Walnut & North St inside SDC; park on Grove St\] 8) Sat 11/14 – Bald Mtn summit (w/optional Headwaters detour, 5.8 miles), 5.1 miles, 1,670 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\]

Please note these routes are subject to change based on the group and weather, as the group does hike in light rains. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky or slippery trails, and layers. Bring water, and if desired, a snack. The group will be limited to 35 participants. 

The hiking series costs $80 (plus a $10 parking fee per visit. Note that the Sugarloaf Annual Pass is $59 and valid at Sugarloaf and Jack London SHP), or free-of-cost for participants with a September 2026 or newer Park Rx from a Sonoma County Medical Provider.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Intro to California Coastal Range Geology
description: Join us and explore Galbreath Preserve. Led by SSU’s Geology instructor Nicole Myers, learn about geologic processes and climatic trends that comprise the natural forces of Northern California, including wildfires, floods and earthquakes. Find out how the California Coast Range was formed by the same geologic events that shaped the Sierra Nevadas and Central Valley of California. Learn how the coastal rocks that we live on made it to California from the deep waters of the central Pacific Ocean, and how those rocks were changed by the forces of plate tectonics.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:
As the days grow shorter and cooler, Sonoma Botanical Garden transforms with the beauty of the changing seasons. From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: Marin Arts & Crafts Show
description:
Marin Arts & Crafts Show returns to the Marin Center Exhibit Hall November 6–8, filling the hall with more than 200 exhibits of fine craft, art and artisan goods. Arriving just as the holiday season gets underway, the three-day market brings together an exciting mix of artists, artisans and craftspeople for a weekend of art, handcraft and seasonal discoveries.

Inspired by the Arts & Crafts movement, the show celebrates craftsmanship, thoughtful design and artistic expression in its many forms. Visitors will find jewelry, ceramics, textiles, glass, woodwork, fine art, furniture, wearable art and specialty foods from artisan food makers. From hand-dyed silks and sculptural ceramics to finely crafted jewelry and heirloom-quality woodworking, the market brings together traditional techniques, fresh ideas and contemporary design.

Throughout the weekend, visitors can talk with artists about their work, watch demonstrations and explore the many forms of handcraft represented at the show. It's a chance to see the details up close, hear how things are made and get to know some of the people behind the work.

The November show brings a festive atmosphere to the Marin Center, with a bustling marketplace of fine crafts, art and artisan foods. Visitors can enjoy wine tasting, sample seasonal treats from specialty food merchants and listen to live music throughout the weekend. Free opportunity drawings offer chances to win wonderful prizes donated by participating artisans, adding to the excitement.

With free admission and free parking, Marin Arts & Crafts Show is an inviting way to spend a fall afternoon with family and friends. As the holidays approach, the market is also a wonderful place to discover distinctive gifts while supporting independent artisans.

**Marin Arts & Crafts Show** November 6–8, 2026 Friday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m. Marin Center Exhibit Hall 20 Avenue of the Flags, San Rafael, CA **Free admission & free parking**

For more information, visit www.MarinArtsAndCraftsShow.com

title: Rituals of Care: Buddhist Chant and Culture
description:
Learn to chant with Chenxing Han and Trent Walker

What is the role of chant in Buddhist practice? How does it shape communities of belonging and cultures of care?

During this daylong, we will engage in a variety of chanting practices from across the Buddhist world, with a special emphasis on the Theravāda tradition as transmitted in mainland Southeast Asia. We’ll explore the musical and textual dimensions of chant, as well as its ritual possibilities. Our charge as a group will be to embody chant as an expression of care for ourselves, our loved ones, and the world.

There will be time to reflect on questions of voice, language, and lineage. Nearly every Buddhist throughout history has engaged in recitation and other practices of aspiration, concentration, and devotion. Our day together invites us into kinship with them as we, too, experience the healing resonances of these practices.

All are warmly welcome to participate; no previous chanting experience is required.

title: Sourdough from Scratch with Monica Flaherty at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description: Join us for a 3-hour hands-on sourdough making class at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, led by Monica Flaherty of the Sebastopol Sourdough Company. Spend three immersive hours in our charming Apple Cottage learning the art and science of sourdough bread making. Monica will walk you through everything you need to know — how wild yeast and fermentation work, why sourdough differs from commercial yeast bread, and how to read your dough. You'll also cover starter care and feeding, mixing and hydration ratios, shaping and scoring techniques, and the secrets to achieving that perfect crust and open crumb. Every guest will leave with an active starter, a feeding schedule and care guide, a shaped dough in a banneton ready to bake at home, and their very own apron to take home as a keepsake. The experience also includes a ride across the farm on our beloved apple-themed trolley to the Apple Cottage.

-Make mortise and tenon joinery with tusk wedges and foxtail wedges.
-Develop the skills and understand the process of building furniture with traditional joinery.

-The focus of the class is learning joinery and developing hand tool skills.
-Please note you may not finish the bench in one weekend. You can complete it at home or join another class as an ongoing student ($120- a day).
Class fee is $325- plus a $35- materials fee ($360- total). All tools are supplied.

Classes are Saturday, 10am to 5pm and Sunday 10am-4pm.

title: You are Invited to North Bay Speech Masters Toastmasters Club Meeting
description:
Whether it's improving our health, focusing on professional advancement, learning a new skill, it is often helpful to obtain someone to help learn new skills like speaking without preparation. The group at Toastmasters can help.

We call speaking without preparation, impromptu speaking. If you want to learn new Impromptu speaking skills, Toastmasters can help. During the meeting, we will practice our impromptu speaking skills during our session we call Table Topics. During the Table Topics, the speaker is given a question, and they are asked to speak for 60 seconds to 2 minutes about the question.

Outside Toastmasters, impromptu speaking happens constantly. You might recognize it in moments such as:

--Being asked for your opinion in a meeting

--Responding to a follow-up question during a presentation

--Introducing yourself or someone else unexpectedly

--Handling a difficult or unplanned question

You can learn tips and tricks about speaking off the cuff at our meeting. Won't you join us and learn

what Toastmasters can do to help you on your professional journey.

Feel free to contact us for the zoon link at our website under the "Contact Us" button. The website is https://3038.toastmastersclubs.org

We hold meetings online and in-person. If joining us in-person, there is limited parking in the front lot. Once in the front door, please sign in at the computer to obtain a visitors' badge. \(IUsually, there is a sheet by the computer telling you how to log in for Toastmasters.\) If the sheet isn't there, the clerk at the desk can help. Then take the elevator down to the second floor, and take a left out of the elevator and a left at the hall and come down to the meeting room.

description:

Nos reuniremos en el estacionamiento del granero blanco (el White Barn) y caminaremos el sendero Meadow mientras escuchamos acerca de la historia cultural de los Wappo en una de sus aldeas ancestral, Wilikos, hoy en día parte de Sugarloaf.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit:  Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Petaluma River Upstream High Tide Paddle
description:
When the tide is high, the Petaluma River opens into a quieter, greener world.

Join The Floathouse crew at their central downtown dock for a gentle, guided paddle upstream, timed to higher tides that allow access beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide into calm, lush stretches of the river that are normally out of reach.

This unhurried paddle highlights the natural beauty of the Petaluma River’s brackish, tidal waterway. Watch for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks, and abundant plant life. The calm water and peaceful surroundings create a deeply grounding experience—many guests say they feel their stress melt away within minutes.

Along the way, knowledgeable guides share stories of the river’s ecology and human history, offering insight into how this upper channel has shaped—and continues to shape—Petaluma. It’s a rare opportunity to experience how close wild nature lives to the heart of downtown.

Beginner-friendly. Sit-on-top kayaks and all gear provided.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Saturdays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? You’ve mastered the basics, now it’s time to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

**What You’ll Learn**

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

**• The Cross Body Lead (CBL) Series:** Master both **Inside and Outside Turns**, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

**• The “I Turn – You Turn”:** A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

**• The Walk-Through:** Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

**• Footwork & Shine:** We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

**Technique & Artistry**

Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

**• The Frame:** Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

**• Upper Body Mechanics:** Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

**• Connection:** Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

**Important Details**

**• No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**• No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

**•** Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

**Saturday 11:00 AM**

Instructor: Lucie Ebnerova

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway #8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

title: Mike Annuzzi
description: If you spent just a few minutes with Mike Annuzzi, you would become aware that his positivity towards life is contagious. Mike is always smiling. He is honest and expresses his feelings openly, probably because he is a Capricorn.  Surrounded by the inspiration from his favorite tour locations, this California native maintains a blend of laid back coastal attitude, hustle of the big city life, drive of Silicon Valley, and refinement and sophistication of wine country.  Mike started playing guitar and writing songs as a child. After the encouragement from friends throughout his high school and college days, he formed and fronted several bands. He discovered his passion in life on a stage performing original music.  He is not the typical Polytechnic University graduate who landed a tech job in Silicon Valley, rather he sewed his roots and paved a path with a musical career. Mike wrote and independently released The One \(2016\), Mike Annuzzi \(2013\), and Paradise \(2012\). In 2013, Mike was chosen West Coast Songwriters International Song Contest Singer/Songwriter of the Year for his single, “Pay No Mind.” He also received Honorable Mention for “You Make Me Fall.” Mike's first single “Paradise” was chosen as West Coast Songwriters San Francisco’s Song of the Year in 2010. His award-winning catalog has been featured on radio around California.  With over 500 shows around the US in the last 3 years headlining clubs, supporting national touring acts, and developing residency performances for venues around California, Mike established himself and his positive rhythmic sound on hometown stages and beyond. He finds himself grateful to have a career around his passion and knows it is attributed to the support of his family, friends, and fans.  Mike is always looking forward, developing his craft as a songwriter and performer, and sharing his positive energy and passion at live shows.  Some stages Mike has been humbled to perform:  BottleRock Napa Valley 2014 with headliners The Cure, Outkast, and Eric Church \(Over 80k tickets sold\) The Mountain Winery, Saratoga CA \(Historic Santa Clara Valley 2k Seat Capacity Outdoor Venue\) The Catalyst, Santa Cruz CA \(Iconic Music Venue host of acts from Neil Young to Nirvana\)  Some of the artists Mike had the opportunity to play events and share stages with include:  Los Lonely Boys \(Single:  “Heaven” Top 20 Billboard Hit\) Kenny Wayne Shepherd, \(“Blue On Black” reached \#1 on Rock Charts\). Colbie Caillat \(Universal Republic Records, Grammy Award Winning Artist\) O.A.R. \(Vangaurd Records\) Edwin McCain \(Singer/Songwriter with Billboard hits including “I'll Be” and “I Could Not Ask For More”\) Lukas Nelson \(Promise of the Real\) Jackie Greene \(Singer/Songwriter and Member of The Black Crowes\) Tyrone Wells \(Independent, iTunes top 10 album artist\)   Here is what others are saying about Mike:  “He sings honestly and expressively and the writing shows sophistication.” -Paul Freeman, Mercury News  “Mike Annuzzi was a pleasure to watch...I loved the positivity of the songs and how full of joy Mike seemed to be filled with.” -Cadet Edac:  iheartsfbands.com  “Well, listening to this wonderful artist it is clear that listeners are in for a treat. His voice is divine and the smoothness of the whole thing just makes me feel alive and gearing to go! Perfect! -Skye McAdams:  The Daily Complains  “Check out this rising star.” -Glen Starkey:  New Times SLO, San Luis Obispo  Mike Annuzzi Plays Godin Guitars Silicon Valley Based Singer/Songwriter, Positive & Rhythmic Music and Lyrics. Check out Singer/Songwriter Mike Annuzzi.

title: We Players: Mountain Goddess Ceremony at Western Hills Garden
description:
Step into the Garden for an immersive ceremony of release, renewal, and connection to past, present, and future.

Conceived and directed by Ava Roy and created and performed by Ling Ling Lee, Mountain Goddess invites participants into a sensory journey through Western Hills Garden. Guided by the Mountain Goddess and her spirited guardians, Ox Head and Horse Face, guests will move through meditation, exploration, ritual, and play—drawing on ancestry, memory, the elements, and the landscape itself.

The experience culminates in a seasonal, culturally relevant meal prepared by acclaimed Sonoma County Chef Sean Quan, featuring Beijing Zhajiangmian-style noodle bar with an array of different vegetables, pickle, and herb garnishes. Wine, beer, non-alcoholic drinks, and cheerful company will also be provided.

Presented by We Players in partnership with Western Hills Garden.

Conceived and Directed by Ava Roy Created and Performed by Ling Ling Lee Costumes by Brooke Jennings

Sliding-scale tickets: $100-200 via We Players website.

Artist Bios:

Ava Roy: Ava is the Founding Artistic Director of We Players, the Bay Area site-integrated theater company she founded in 2000. For more than two decades, she has created immersive performances that bring audiences into new relationships with landscape, history, and place, including collaborations with the National Park Service, California State Parks, and San Francisco Recreation and Parks. Roy is a graduate of Stanford University, where she designed her own major, Ritual and Performance in Aesthetic Education.

Ling Ling Lee: Ling Ling is a San Francisco-born multidisciplinary artist with a background in Chinese theater and dance. A graduate of San Francisco School of the Arts and Shanghai Theatre Academy, Lee works across theater, dance, storytelling, and fire performance. Her collaborators include We Players, Meow Wolf, Disney, Kaimera Wanderbeasts, and the European Juggling Convention. With We Players, Lee has performed as Ox Head/Horse Face in Psychopomp and appeared in Macbeth at Fort Point and Odyssea.

Brooke Jennings: Brooke is an award-winning costume designer working in the Bay Area and beyond and a graduate of UC Santa Cruz’s Theater Arts master’s program. Her credits include work with San Francisco Playhouse, Shotgun Players, San Jose Stage, Crowded Fire Theater Company, and We Players. Jennings began designing for We Players in 2015 with Ondine at Sutro, for which she received a Theater Bay Area Award for Outstanding Costume Design, and has since become the company’s resident costume designer and a longtime creative collaborator.

Jaz Sufi (she/hers) is a queer Iranian-American poet and arts educator. She is the author of *Catalog of Shadows* (Game Over Books). Her work has been published in Best New Poets, Best of the Net, AGNI, Black Warrior Review, Muzzle, and elsewhere. She is a National Poetry Slam finalist and has received fellowships from Kundiman, the Watering Hole, and New York University, where she received her MFA. Chapbook Prize (June 2025) and Write Bloody Publishing’s 2024 Jack McCarthy Book Prize (September 2025) for *Sand Bodied Florida Boy.* IG: @graysonwritespoems www.graysonwritespoems.com

Gary Weiner moved to Sonoma County in 1973 and now resides in Sebastopol. title: Napa Primary Care Conference November 4-8, 2026
description:
The Napa Primary Care Conference is a unique educational conference for physicians and medical professionals who care for active and athletic patients or who themselves lead such a lifestyle.

16 HOURS AAFP CME CREDIT

Location

The conference will be held at The Napa Valley Marriott Resort and Spa, conveniently located within minutes of renowned wineries, shopping, attractions, and numerous options for exercise and physical activity.

Course Description

This conference will present very practical information that you can use in your practice. Topics will include common medical and musculoskeletal problems that affect patients who lead an active lifestyle. The focus will be on providing information that will help you diagnose and manage these conditions in the office; so that you can help your patients get moving again and improve their performance. In addition, various topics on healthy lifestyles and personal wellness will make this conference a valuable experience for all attendees.

Intended Audience

The curriculum is directed to Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Emergency Medicine, PM and R and Orthopedics specialists as well as Physical Therapists, Athletic Trainers, Physicians Assistants, Nurse Practitioners and others who want to earn Continuing Medical Education from leading physician experts who are outstanding speakers.

Course Learning Objectives

Upon conclusion of this program, participants should be able to:

1. Describe recent advances regarding various medical problems and their impact on the athlete and exercise performance.

2. Identify current recommendations for proper nutrition in active and athletic patients.

3. Illustrate key skills in the diagnosis and management of common musculoskeletal problems encountered by family physicians.

4. Diagnose common problems encountered by patients and effectively treat these conditions.

5. Define common medical-legal issues relevant to the primary care physician.

We hope you can join us for this unique conference in 2024. I look forward to meeting you in Napa!

description:
Experience a full day and night of live music in Point Reyes Station as Ryan MacNeill & The Big Deal and JeConte take over the legendary Old Western Saloon on Saturday, November 7.

Ryan MacNeill & The Big Deal kick things off from 4:00–7:00pm, bringing their blend of Cosmic Americana, rock & roll, country, and psychedelic roots music to one of West Marin’s most iconic stages.

Fronted by Ryan MacNeill, the band pairs traditional songwriting with expansive guitar textures, rich vocal harmonies, driving basslines, swirling organ, and dynamic rhythms. Their music moves easily between open-road Americana and exploratory, psychedelic jams—grounded in the traditions of American roots music while pushing well beyond them.

The evening continues from 8:00–11:00pm with JeConte, featuring rock & roll harmonica and special guest Archer Monk. The all star band includes Matt Allard on organ, Jono on bass, Adam Bowers on slide guitar, and Andrew Tuckman on drums.

Set in the heart of Point Reyes Station, it’s an afternoon and evening of live music, good times, and West Marin character at the Old Western Saloon, brought to you by Wild West Ferments.

Artist Statement

Gabriel’s work stems from the intersection of ecology and queer identity, and the parallel frameworks they provide for resisting rigid categories, binary distinctions, and expected outcomes. Burgeon examines the notion that transformation does not require resolution. The work draws inspiration from natural processes of growth and consumption, and the way they blur the boundaries between organism and environment, individual and collective. Constructing clay forms through an extended process of repetition and accumulation, pattern and deviation, Gabriel’s work explores the idea that to be in flux is not to be incomplete.

title: Callie Watts
description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. title: Wine Country Marine Corps Birthday Ball
description:
Brigadier General Andrew T. Priddy, Commanding General of the 1st Marine Division, based at Camp Pendleton in Southern California, will be Guest of Honor at Wine Country Marines’ 2026 Marine Corps Birthday Ball. The November 7 event at Jacuzzi Family Vineyards will celebrate the Corps’ 251st birthday.

Sonoma Valley’s annual event began in 1985. A formal Marine Corps Birthday Ball is an unusual gathering for a community as small as Sonoma, and its setting in the heart of California Wine Country has helped it become known as a “Destination Ball,” drawing Marines from across the country.

The local event is part of the worldwide Marine Corps Birthday Ball tradition honoring the Corps’ founding on November 10, 1775. Marines gather around that date each year to celebrate their shared history and service.

A career infantry officer and 1995 U.S. Naval Academy graduate, Priddy assumed command of the division in May 2026. His participation continues Sonoma Valley’s history of welcoming distinguished military guests.

Founded by local Marines and their supporters, the Sonoma Valley event brings generations together around an enduring conviction: “Once a Marine. Always a Marine.” The evening reflects a lifelong commitment to fellow Marines and the community that welcomes them.

The celebration supports Wine Country Marines’ work assisting service members, veterans and their families through hardship. Military families, veterans and friends of the Corps are invited to join the November 7 gathering. Explore tickets and reservations at WineCountryMarines.org.

title: Dublinesque Album Release Party
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Don't miss this special evening where we’ll take a musical trip to Dublin with some of the Bay Area’s finest musicians and singers! Eamonn Flynn, Darcy Noonan, Hector Bragado and Felim Egan will dazzle us with their traditional and original "Dublinesque" harmonies. OCA favorites through and through, we're just delighted to bring back this spirited, talented group.
Tickets are $25, $20 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM. Refreshments available, art gallery open during intermission.
Get Tickets
EAMONN FLYNN & DUBLINESQUE
Eamonn Flynn forges his own brand of Irish soul. The Dublin-born singer-songwriter/pianist got his start with The Commitments, a hit film about an Irish soul band, and has since worked with American blues and R&B stars Elvin Bishop, Maria Muldaur, Evelyn Champagne King, Michael Franti & Spearhead, Zigaboo Modeliste (The Meters), The Ray Charles Project, and many more.
​
Flynn's new quartet DUBLINESQUE brings his deep soul and gospel roots together with the Irish music traditions he was raised on.
​
"Dublinesque is my attempt to recreate the kind of parties we had in my parent's house, growing up in Dublin," explains Flynn. "There'd be neighbours and friends and it would always end up as a sing-song/jam session. Everyone would participate - if you couldn't hold a tune you'd perform a 'recitation' or tell a joke!
​
"There was never any delineation between genres of music - whether it was Irish tunes and ballads, soul music or a Beatles song," he emphasizes.
​
The band brings together three talented Bay Area Irish traditional musicians: fellow Irishman Félim Egan (The Black Brothers) on accordion, local favorite Darcy Noonan on fiddle, and from Basque country, Spain, Hector Bragado on banjo. They are also sometimes joined by special guests. Previous guests have included Glide Memorial Choir, Maria Muldaur, Mary Black, Róisín O, Michael Black, Shay Black, Autumn Rhodes, Margaret Graham and dancers from the Kennelly, Dillon and Whelan Schools of Irish Dance and the Cooley-Keegan Branch of Comhaltas Ceoltóirí.
​
"This is my chance to play with some of my favorite musicians and recreate those parties!" says Flynn.
​
Flynn's latest of three solo albums is 'Anywhere But Home,' celebrating Dublin from his San Francisco pandemic perspective. It received praise and widespread airplay in the US, Canada, Europe and Australia.
"Flynn's songwriting moves with true emotional register across history, folklore and poetry…with grit and true Dublin savvy.” Deirdre Cronin - Irish Music Magazine

title: True West
description: Set in a suburban California home, True West follows two brothers with sharply contrasting personalities who reunite while house-sitting for their mother. One is a disciplined, aspiring screenwriter, while the other lives a more nomadic and unpredictable life. As they reconnect, their interactions shift from uneasy familiarity to intense competition, fueled by conflicting ambitions and long-standing tensions. Shepard's play delves into themes of authenticity, creativity, and the myth of the American frontier, using sharp dialogue and dark humor to reveal the instability beneath the surface of everyday life. As the brothers' dynamic evolves, the boundaries between their identities begin to blur, raising questions about who they are and what defines them.

title: Illeagles
description:
What do people want when they go see a live band? The members of SF Bay Area–based tribute band Illeagles believe audiences want to be fully engaged and captivated from the first note to the final encore. After more than a year of sold-out performances, that belief has proven true night after night. .

Illeagles was founded in late 2016 when six friends came together with two things in common: a deep love for timeless West Coast rock and a shared commitment to musical excellence. Each member is a standout musician in their own right, and that collective passion led to countless hours of study, rehearsal, and refinement — carefully recreating the signature harmonies, soaring guitar lines, and tight ensemble interplay that defined a generation of classic American rock. From high-octane rock anthems to heartfelt, harmony-driven ballads, Illeagles delivers a dynamic set that blends faithful musical craftsmanship with their own swagger, energy, and stage presence. It’s common for audiences to start singing along from the very first song and keep going until the lights come up — or their voices give out.

title: Nancy Fawson Music
description:
Nancy Fawson is a powerhouse Bay Area-based vocalist and songwriter whose musical roots run deep in soul, R&B and rock. Raised on the iconic sounds of Sam Cooke, Etta James, Aretha Franklin, Chaka Khan, Stevie Wonder, and Amy Winehouse, Nancy’s musical influences have left an indelible imprint on her voice and style. With a unique, soulful tone and a passion for heartfelt expression, Nancy connects with her audience on a profound level—delivering each song with purity, emotion, and authenticity.

Nancy’s vocal range spans across a variety of genres, including soul, funk, blues, R&B, and rock, allowing her to bring versatility to every performance. Whether performing with a duo or full band, she engages audiences with her compelling stage presence and soulful delivery.

As the lead singer of the popular Marin-based blues, soul, and funk band Corner Pocket, Nancy continues to captivate crowds with her raw energy and dedication to the craft. In addition to live performances, she is also available for recording session work, offering her talents as both a lead and background vocalist.

With a sound that blends classic influences with modern flair, Nancy Fawson is an artist whose voice you won’t soon forget.

title: STIMULANT | Art Exhibition and Events
description:
Apocalypse Studio, Sebastopol’s multidisciplinary father-and-daughter artist duo, presents STIMULANT: Art as Remedy for Diseased Culture, a two-week exhibition of large-scale paintings and digital works at Laguna Lab, November 7–20, 2026. The show opens Saturday, November 7 at 7.30 PM with a spoken word performance featuring the exhibition’s centerpiece, a 144 piece mosaic – The Oversoul. 
STIMULANT argues that only culture can rebalance our dysfunctional systems of money and power. The exhibition explores the inner and outer work of co-creating that new culture: art, ideas, and dialogue that stimulates new possibilities and activates action. 
Over two weeks the exhibition comes alive through two live performances, two artist lectures, a salon, and six afternoons to meet the artists for conversation and walkthroughs.

title: STIMULANT: Art as Remedy for Diseased Culture, Exhibition and Events
description: In a diseased society with failing systems, what can we do to turn things around? For two weeks a new exhibition from Sonoma County’s own Apocalypse Studio, a father and daughter artist duo, *STIMULANT: Art as Remedy for Diseased Culture* proposes that art is the antidote and creativity is the countermove. This exhibition explores the inner and outer work of co-creating that antidote: art that stimulates society’s creativity - the social sculpture we all create together. There will be two performances, two lectures, a Parisian -style Art Salon, and times to visit the large exhibition and talk with the artists. All events are free to attend. Visit www.apocalypse.art/stimulant for details and schedule of events.
source: Creative Sonoma, North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

title: Sweeney Todd
description:
Sweeney Todd is largely considered one of Stephen Sondheim’s masterpieces. With it, he aimed to create a musical that could “scare the hell out of everyone,” and yet, somehow, be funny.

The story centers around Sweeney Todd, an unjustly exiled barber who returns to London, seeking vengeance against the lecherous judge who framed him and ravaged his young wife. The road to revenge leads Todd to Mrs. Lovett, a resourceful proprietress of a failing pie shop, above which, he opens a new barber practice. Mrs. Lovett’s luck sharply shifts when Todd’s thirst for blood inspires the integration of an ingredient into her meat pies that has the people of 19th Century London lining up…and the carnage has only just begun!

\***Content Advisory:** Adult language and violent themes, as well as controversial pie recipes. Recommended for 12+.

Where there’s a will, there’s a way.

“The Book of Will” brings to life the chaotic, hilarious, passionate, and mostly true endeavor to compile Shakespeare’s plays into the legendary First Folio!

About the show: Without William Shakespeare, we wouldn’t have literary masterpieces like “Romeo and Juliet.” But without Henry Condell and John Heminges, we would have lost half of Shakespeare’s plays forever! After the death of their friend and mentor, the two actors are determined to compile the First Folio and preserve the words that shaped their lives. They’ll just have to borrow, beg, and band together to get it done. Amidst the noise and color of Elizabethan London, The Book of Will finds an unforgettable true story of love, loss, and laughter, and sheds new light on a man you may think you know.

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

title: Self-Compassion for Shame: Practical Skills for Emotional Wellbeing
description:
with Christopher Germer and Carolina Bautista-Velez

What’s wrong with you? Who do you think you are?

All humans can experience shame—including the most practiced meditators and meditation teachers. It can even happen when we’re entirely innocent of wrongdoing, as well as when we make a mistake. Whenever we feel bad about ourselves, for whatever reason, there’s usually a touch of shame present. It strikes us at the core of our being and yet has nothing to do with who we really are.

The power of shame is largely an illusion. As meditation teacher Tara Brach says, shame often masquerades as a “trance of unworthiness” that gets its power from our instinctive avoidance of it. However, when we look at shame through the eyes of self-compassion, we can discover something quite surprising—that shame is an innocent emotion arising from a universal wish to be loved. This insight opens the door to compassion and self-understanding. Research shows that self-compassion is the opposite of shame. As self-compassion goes up, shame goes down.

In this benefit workshop, Chris Germer and Carolina Bautista-Velez present the practice of Self-Compassion for Shame, specifically tailored to loosen the grip of shame in our own lives. The workshop includes short talks, exercises, practices, and discussion. Participants will learn 5-6 simple tools to bring home to use in their daily life.

All are invited to attend this benefit with the awareness that shame can be a difficult human emotion—and that self-compassion itself can be emotionally activating. The workshop may be emotionally challenging, so some familiarity with practicing self-compassion before joining this workshop may be helpful.

Experienced self-compassion teachers will be available as mentors, in-person and online, to provide information or emotional support to participants, as needed.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

SoulCollage® is part creative exploration and part self-discovery. It’s fun and can be delightfully surprising! Participants will explore the process of collage making using magazines images on 5” x 8” canvas, usually cut from mat board or other stiff paper. Collage allows everyone to be an artist, even if you don’t believe you have a creative bone in your body, because you are working with found images. In this Introductory class you will also explore the intuitive process of "listening" to the wisdom of the collage you completed, using images that you were drawn to. title: True West
description: Set in a suburban California home, True West follows two brothers with sharply contrasting personalities who reunite while house-sitting for their mother. One is a disciplined, aspiring screenwriter, while the other lives a more nomadic and unpredictable life. As they reconnect, their interactions shift from uneasy familiarity to intense competition, fueled by conflicting ambitions and long-standing tensions. Shepard's play delves into themes of authenticity, creativity, and the myth of the American frontier, using sharp dialogue and dark humor to reveal the instability beneath the surface of everyday life. As the brothers' dynamic evolves, the boundaries between their identities begin to blur, raising questions about who they are and what defines them.

title: Book Launch: Heart Stories by Dennis von Elgg
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Please join us for a special groundbreaking book launch featuring Harmony Village’s own Dennis von Elgg, owner of The Redwood Needle Acupuncture Studio. This is a free event featuring selected readings by the author, audience Q&A, book sales and signing. Refreshments available. The book’s expected release date is September 1, 2026.
In
Heart Stories
, acupuncturist, educator, and Sonoma Coast author Dennis von Elgg explores the fascinating intersection of Traditional Chinese Medicine, modern cardiovascular science, and the stories we carry that shape our lives. Drawing on decades of clinical experience, contemporary medical research, timeless Eastern wisdom, and moments from his own journey, von Elgg invites readers to consider heart disease through an entirely new lens—one that recognizes the intimate relationship between physiology, emotion, stress, memory, and consciousness.
Rather than presenting Eastern and Western medicine as opposing viewpoints,
Heart Stories
reveals the surprising places where they converge. Along the way, readers encounter compelling patient stories, reflections from the author’s own life, practical insights for improving cardiovascular health, and an exploration of the emotional patterns that often accompany illness, resilience, and healing.
Written for both healthcare practitioners and thoughtful readers,
Heart Stories
is an exploration of what it means to heal—not only the physical heart, but the human heart as well. Blending science, philosophy, personal reflection, and clinical wisdom, it offers an invitation to see both health and human experience with fresh eyes.
"Drawing from decades of hard-won clinical experience, von Elgg reframes our tradition while respecting its roots, considering the classics in the context of modern research and cardiovascular therapy. With case studies that read like stories and invitations for us to reflect on both ourselves and our patients, this is one of those books that will make going to work all the more interesting and rewarding."
Dr. Jason D. Robertson - Seattle Institute of East Asian Medicine
"This work bridges the measurable and the mysterious aspects of the heart with remarkable intelligence and humanity. Rooted in both cardiovascular science and Chinese medicine, it offers a rare synthesis — equally rigorous and deeply compassionate. Professor von Elgg offers a beautifully articulated exploration of what it truly means for the heart to be 'well.'"
Dr. Bianca Di Giulio,
L.Ac
.
Author of "Bridging the Gap: Integrative Oncology and the Practice of Traditional Chinese Medicine"
"In 'Heart Stories,' Dennis von Elgg turns his holistic lens towards cardiology while finding deeper meaning and enjoyment in our lives. This book is a written treasure that will inform and delight practitioners and patients alike for many generations to come."
Robyn Adcock, DACM, LAc, CMT, Director of Pediatric Integrative Medicine, UCSF
"It is unusual for a book to give both the EKG and the 神 (shén) equal weight. With clinical clarity and a teacher's warmth, Dennis' book makes the case for psychocardiology and a way to meet the whole of a patient's being. For practitioners working where biomedicine and East Asian medicine meet, it's a thoughtful map of a territory that is too often left unexplored."
Toby Daly, PhD, LAc
Author of An Introduction to Chinese Medicine, The Saam Acupuncture Tradition, and Tracing Our Lineage
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Dennis von Elgg,
L.Ac
., is an acupuncturist, educator, and author who has spent more than three decades exploring the intersection of Traditional Chinese Medicine, modern medical science, and the human experience. Living and practicing on California’s Sonoma Coast, he has dedicated his career to helping patients understand the relationship between emotional well-being, cardiovascular health, and the body’s remarkable capacity to heal.
His debut book,
Heart Stories: An Inner Exploration of Heart Disease and Human Consciousness
, weaves together clinical insight, contemporary research, Eastern philosophy, patient stories, and reflections from his own life to offer a fresh perspective on the Heart—not only as an organ, but as a center of physiology, emotion, and consciousness.
Dennis lives on the Sonoma Coast, where he maintains a private acupuncture practice, teaches, writes, practices yoga, coaches high school baseball, and treasures time with his son.
Through his writing, Dennis hopes to encourage a deeper conversation about healing—one that honors both scientific discovery and the wisdom found in our own lived experience, reminding us that the journey toward health is as much about understanding ourselves as it is about understanding the body.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting in Santa Rosa
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

Blending the fascinating history of one of America’s most prolific and successful writers with the serenity of nature, Jack London State Historic Park offers more than 29 miles of back-country trails that roam through mixed forests, redwood groves, oak woodlands, and grassy meadows in Sonoma County’s Valley of the Moon.  

Active duty or retired military identification or form DD214 can be presented at the entry kiosk to receive free admission.

Admission, regularly priced at $15, covers one vehicle of up to nine passengers for the day.  Park hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily.

**Talasana Krama (Foundational Sequence) & Pranayama**
**Mondays 9-10:30am - Songbird Cotati - RSVP**
**$25, Discounted Class Passes & Sliding Scale Available**
Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.
