For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Ryan Martin

Date: Monday, November 9th

Time: 12:30PM-2PM

Location: Santa Rosa Store

Free!


Class 2 of 3: Watercolour Blooms – Landscape -This is number two in a series of three classes using Winsor & Newton Professional Watercolour with artist Ryan Martin. Attend all three to learn week-by-week from Ryan but none are prerequisites if your schedule does not allow. In this 90-minute session, artist Ryan will show you how to paint a luminous mountain and lake landscape using wet-into-wet watercolour techniques and masking fluid to preserve crisp highlights. You’ll learn how to encourage watercolour blooms as pigments spread, soften, and separate, creating misty mountains, glowing skies, and shimmering reflections. Winsor & Newton Art Masking Fluid will be used to save bright whites for snow, light, and sparkle, making the scene feel alive and atmospheric. Minimal drawing experience is required -this class is all about understanding timing, water, and pigment to create beautiful, expressive landscapes with confidence. All supplies are provided, so you can try different pigments, colors, and brushes and discover what you enjoy using. Ryan will also be available after class to answer questions and help you choose materials to keep exploring at home.


Limited seats available—reserve your spot today!


Ryan Martin lives and works in the San Francisco Bay Area where he attended the California College of the Arts. Through painting and drawing, Martin creates surreal, dream-like compositions of his subjects. He is influenced by his Native American (Mexican/Seri) and Russian heritage through painting reinterpretations of war bonnets and kokoshniks haloing his subjects. Martin’s artwork has been highlighted by numerous media including The Advocate, Creative Boom, The Art of Man and others. He has exhibited widely across the United States, including the deYoung Museum, Mark Wolfe Contemporary, Modern Eden Gallery of San Francisco, Elizabeth Houston Gallery of NYC, as well as numerous fairs including SCOPE, Untitled Art in Miami and Volta NY.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and Connection: 11/10/26 — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and Connection: November 10th, 2026

  
    
      
        
          $15.00
        
      
    
  

Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and ConnectionTuesday, November 10th, 4:00-5:30pm The practice of “poem making” offers a means to express the metaphors and meaning of the joys and suffering we experience in ourselves and bear witness to in others. Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is true in our hearts  and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a "poet" or even a "writer" to allow words and feelings to pour through your pen. Redwing Keyssar has been leading "Poetic Medicine in Community" sessions through her work in Palliative Care at UCSF for the past 6 years. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped "wounded healers," and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths.Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens!This is an IN-PERSON gathering to establish a strong and safe creative community. We are all poets!No Materials Required, Reading Material Provided. Personal writing materials encouraged. 22 students maximum. About the Instructor: Judith Redwing Keyssar, RN has traversed an amazing 35+ year journey in the healing arts/healthcare. Redwing is an educator, end-of-life doula, author, poet, song-writer, ceremonialist, national presenter and frequent contributor to public issues about Palliative and End of Life Care. Redwing is currently the Director of Education at the MERI Center for Education in Palliative Care at UCSF/Mt. Zion. Her professional career includes being the Clinical Director at Zen Hospice Project and the Director of Palliative Care and Nursing at Jewish Family and Children’s Services from 2004-2018. She is a founder and adjunct faculty member of the California State University Shiley/Haynes Institute of Palliative Care, and has taught courses at OLLI at Sonoma State. Redwing is the author of an award-winning book, “Last Acts of Kindness; Lessons for the Living from the Bedsides of the Dying” and is the recipient of numerous awards in the field of Palliative Care. After studying with John Fox at the Institute for Poetic Medicine, her passion for using poetry as a healing modality has led to the development of a successful international program in Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and Connection, through her work at the UCSF MERI Center. Learn more about her here: https://redwingkeyssar.com/

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Let’s Tap! Beginner - Advanced on Tuesdays
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Welcome to the wonderful world of Tap!
These classes are for those who wish to discover tap dance and those who wish to continue exploring.
This class offering is weekly on Tuesdays in six-week sessions. Three levels are taught: Beginner from 10:15-11 AM, Intermediate from 11 AM - 12 Noon and Advanced from 12:30-1:30 PM. Summer Session starts Tuesday, September 8th and ends Tuesday, October 13. Additional classes can be taken on the same day for $5/class (pay on site).
Classes are led by
Starr Hergenrather and Gabe Copeland
. A limited supply of
tap shoes is available for use at the class.
Please contact us ahead of time to ensure we have the right size for you.
Participation fee is $120 for the series (six sessions), $90 for OCA members.
You can
email us
with any questions, or come to a class.
Register
Tap Dance provides an avenue for developing coordination, balance, musicality, rhythm, and general love for movement. We will learn the basics (if a beginner) and beyond, through warm-ups, discover the language of tap dance, learn the Shim Sham, and routines that will launch you onto your own exploration of the dance form.
Tap is an extremely fun and rewarding form of dance. Tap Dance originated in the 19th century through a fusion of African and Irish dance styles, becoming a unique American art form in the melting pot of New York City. It developed through percussive footwork, initially on plantations and in urban cellars, and later gained widespread popularity through minstrel shows, vaudeville, and Hollywood musicals. Innovators like
Bill "Bojangles" Robinson
, the
Nicholas Brothers
, Eleanor Powell, Fred Astaire, Gene Kelly to name just a few, who shaped its evolution, which continues today with new fusions in contemporary dance.
May 26
, Bojangle’s birthday, is National
Tap Dance Day.
Starr Hergenrather
has been teaching Theatre and Dance for over 54 years, dancing for 70 years, which is amazing since she is only 45 years old! She received her Theatre Arts and Teaching Credentials in 1971 from Denver, CO. Starr has taught theatre/creative dramatics/improvisation/dance to all ages and directed and produced theatre for many, many years. She and her family moved to Sebastopol in 1983. In 1987, she received her Dance credential and degree from SSU. Starr loves the theatre and dance and everything about them. She has performed on stage and in film throughout her teaching career. Before joining the staff at Analy in 2001 where she became the Theatre Arts Program Director and taught one dance class starting in 2010, when the high school lost its Dance instructor due to No Child Left Behind, she taught at Brookhaven School from 1990-2001 teaching a myriad of subjects, including Theatre and Dance, and Rincon Valley Junior High School from 1987-1997, as BJ Van Noy’s choreographer and asst. director of her Music Program. Starr’s tap mentor was a Vaudeville and later Broadway song and Dance man by the name of Jack Williams. Starr studied with Jack for almost 20 years., until his waning years.
Tap, which is a magical form of dance, btw, is Starr’s first dance love, next to swing, salsa, and partner dancing, and then just plain social, wild hippie dancing at concerts.
Starr also teaches Private Tap Lessons for any level dancer. Starr has a studio at her home.
Gabe Copeland (pictured with Mindy on flier above)
Gabe has been a dance educator for over 20 years. He has performed nationally and internationally as a featured member of the Los Angeles based touring company Rhapsody in Taps. Other credits include ABC’s Gong Show, China’s Dream television show, soloist in KIN Dance Company’s Down Around Brown Town and soloist on an international tour with Caution: Men At Work Tap! He has also performed in many Southern California Civic Light Opera productions such as Cole, Crazy For You, and Rodgers & Hart: A Celebration. Most recently, Gabe performed in the critically acclaimed Jazz Tap Jam! Show for the Lively Arts Foundation honoring Gregory Hines and had the privilege of performing a piece originally choreographed by the tap legend himself.
Mindy Copeland
As a dance educator since 1995, Mindy has also enjoyed a career in performance. As a member of the Los Angeles based touring company, Rhapsody in Taps, Mindy performed the choreography of Linda Sohl-Ellison, Gregory Hines, Fred Strickler, Sam Weber, Brenda Bufalino and Foster Johnson. She was a featured soloist in the international tour of Caution: Men At Work Tap! Mindy appeared in the short film, Tap Heat with choreography by Danny Daniels, and appeared in and choreographed for national and international television shows including the Jerry Lewis Telethon, China’s Dream Show, Spain’s Extremo Urbano, and ABC’s Gong Show. Other stage credits include, appearing with the legendary Chester Whitmore in A Tribute to Jeni Le Gon, and KIN Dance Company’s James Brown tribute show, Down Around Brown Town. Most recently, Mindy directed and performed in the critically acclaimed 2023 Jazz Tap Jam! Show for the Lively Arts Foundation.
The Copelands
have shared the stage with tap legends Dianne Walker, Arthur Duncan, Fayard Nicholas and Bob Carroll and performed Begin the Beguine together in Swing Into Spring. They direct
Tap Overload
which has a collection of original tap dance ﬁlm shorts on its YouTube channel and produced an original tap dance comedy show-
Office Beat.
The show received rave reviews and the official Hollywood Fringe Festival Award, Best of Physical theatre and Dance as well as the Robby Award for Best Choreography of LA Theatre in 2016.

location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Join us for Abstract Watercolor Painting at Riley Street, Santa Rosa

Instructor: Anne Millett

Date: Tuesday, November 10th

Time: 11:00AM-2:30PM

Fee: $45.00


There will be over 70 high quality paint colors for you to choose from, plus 6 metallics. You will spend time selecting your colors intuitively, for the way they make you feel in the moment. This process is quite personal.

What we paint does not need to accurately represent real things that we see in the "outside world". We listen to our intuitions as our paintings build shape by shape, mark by mark, without planning the end result. We paint simply and methodically, focusing on putting paint on paper and seeing what happens, then where we'll go next.

High quality watercolor paint, very good brushes, 1 piece of Arches 140# cold press watercolor paper (and a second if you finish your first painting), and complete set-ups for painting in class will be provided.


This class is designed for adults 18+

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: The Kabbalah of Meaning
description:
Jewish Wisdom for a Life That Matters

No matter how much we achieve, something within us still asks: “Is this it? Isn’t there something more?”

The Kabbalah of Meaning is a new six-session JLI course exploring the Jewish answer to that question. What are we really searching for—and where can it be found?

Drawing on Kabbalah and centuries of Jewish wisdom, we’ll uncover the essential building blocks of a deeply meaningful life. We’ll explore how purpose can be found in our work, relationships, challenges, accomplishments, and even the ordinary routines that fill our days.

You don’t have to revamp your life. You don’t need to meditate on a mountaintop. You simply need a new lens through which to see the rich world of meaning already woven into every part of your life.

Thoughtful, practical, and surprisingly relevant, this course offers fresh perspectives and useful tools for living with greater clarity, connection, and intention.

title: Poetry Book Club: If Not, Winter: Fragments of Sappho by Sappho/Anne Carson
description: Each month, the Poetry Book Club meets online to discuss one must-read book of poems, whether a timeless classic or an award-winning contemporary. Led by Napa poet Kathleen Patterson, who has been an enthusiastic book club member since its beginning, meetings are open to all levels of poetry readers, both the curious and the committed. ABOUT THE BOOK In this "gorgeous translation" \(The New York Times\), one of our most fearless and original poets provides a tantalizing window onto the genius of a woman whose lyric power spans millennia. Of the nine books of lyrics the ancient Greek poet Sappho is said to have composed, only one poem has survived complete. The rest are fragments. In this miraculous new translation, acclaimed poet and classicist Anne Carson presents all of Sappho’s fragments, in Greek and in English, as if on the ragged scraps of papyrus that preserve them, inviting a thrill of discovery and conjecture that can be described only as electric—or, to use Sappho’s words, as “thin fire ... racing under skin.” "Carson is in many ways \[Sappho's\] ideal translator.... Her command of language is hones to a perfect edge and her approach to the text, respectful yet imaginative, results in verse that lets Sappho shine forth." —Los Angeles Times ABOUT THE AUTHOR ANNE CARSON was born in Canada and has been a professor of Classics for over thirty years. Her awards and honors include the Lannan Award, the Pushcart Prize, the Griffin Trust Award for Excellence in Poetry, and fellowships from the Guggenheim and MacArthur Foundations.

title: Sound Bath with Laura Benson
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Rest & Renew at our Sound Bath!
Support your nervous system, release anxiety and stress, and harmonize your body, mind and spirit on the 2nd Tuesday of every month! Laura Benson has a Masters in Intuition Medicine(R) and is a certified sound healer who will guide you through a gentle meditation before each sound bath session. Bring your own yoga mat & blanket and come ready to rest and renew! In the OCA Studio.
Sliding scale pricing $25-$35.
Register
A sound bath is a whole-body, immersive listening experience. During a sound bath, participants often sit or lie down, and are surrounded by the mostly non-melodic soundscapes created by a range of instruments played by the sound bath facilitator. Hence, they are “bathed” in sound.
Sound therapy is a non-invasive healing modality that utilizes the physical and physiological interactions of sound on our bodies and nervous systems to produce therapeutic results. In a sound healing session, specific sonic frequencies are used to soothe the central nervous system, calm the breath, and quiet the mind by encouraging the brain to move into more relaxed states, down from beta (fight-or-flight) and into theta and alpha waves. This increases present-moment awareness and reduces stress and anxiety. Sound baths have been found to be effective in improving mood, cognitive function, and overall mental, physical, and spiritual wellbeing.
Crystal bowl sound baths are particularly powerful in that each bowl is tuned to a specific frequency that corresponds with a different chakra, or energy center, of the body. Based on specific needs, a practitioner can focus on releasing tension or clearing out stuck energy in specific chakras by playing certain bowls or intervals.
While attending a sound bath, you may experience physical sensations brought out by the crystal sound bowls or gong, such as tingling in your limbs or scalp, slowing of your breathing, eye flutters, or small muscle spasms. Not to worry! These sensations often indicate the release of tension or emotional energy stored in the body’s energy systems.

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Nature Journaling Workshop
description:
Connect with local plants and wildlife during this guided Nature Journaling Workshop at Lake Solano Park! Guests will learn tips and tricks for nature journaling, and receive a guided tour of the Native Plant Demonstration Garden. 

Planted in early 2025, this new garden features species that are important for Putah Creek wildlife and have cultural value. Funded by a grant from the California Coastal Conservancy, it is a collaborative project between Solano Resource Conservation District, Putah Creek Council, Solano County Parks, and Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation. 

Putah Creek Council will provide a variety of art supplies and guide books, however, guests are highly encouraged to bring their own journal. Guests may also wish to bring their own chair as seating is limited in the garden.

The workshop will take place on Wednesday, November 11th from 1PM – 3PM, led by Maddie Galal, Project Manager at Putah Creek Council and Vice President of the California Native Plant Society- Willis L Jepson \(Solano\) Chapter. Registration is required, where you will receive detailed directions a few days prior to the event. 

Note that parking at Lake Solano Park is $8 for all visitors. This event is open to all ages, but is best suited for those ages 12 and older.

title: Author Event: A Murderous Vintage by Paul Wagner
description: Join us for a special event with Paul Wagner, author of A Murderous Vintage. This event is free, but we appreciate your RSVP below so we can plan for your attendance. ABOUT THE BOOK There are lots of characters in the Napa Valley, from iconoclastic winemakers to the many lesser lights who make those wines possible. They are not all likeable people. But only one of them ends up dead in a tank of fermenting Pinot noir. And Alex Stone, the young editor of the local paper, is in the right place at the right time. Or is he?  "Paul Wagner shows that he knows Napa Valley, the world of wine and how to tell a good, fun story. A Murderous Vintage is a pleasure for both wine and mystery lovers. It grabs readers quickly because of the intriguing mystery, the quirky characters and because it transports you to Napa and wine country. It's a vacation with a mystery, you just need your own glass of wine." — Rick Kushman, NY Times bestselling author "Harvest time in Napa Valley: When a winemaker who has made his share of enemies is discovered floating in a tank of new Pinot Noir, the bike-riding owner, publisher, editor, and reporter of the small but scrappy Rutherford Record sets out to discover the truth. His quest uncovers a secret that not only wrecks his favorite mode of transportation but catapults his livelihood -- and his life -- into dire peril. Many people are inspired to write about Napa Valley, but few know it and the world of wine as Paul Wagner does. His insight underscores every passage of his lively page-turner, filled with engaging characters, baffling riddles and a great deal of fun. Oh, yes, and there is wine." — Sasha Paulsan, Napa Journalist and author ABOUT THE AUTHOR Paul Wagner was named the McPherson Distinguished Teacher at Napa Valley College and has taught in the Viticulture and Enology department there for more than thirty years. He is a guest lecturer at many universities, including CETYS in Mexico and the Wintour MBA program in Europe, and has won many international awards for his work in the wine industry. His books, including, Wine Marketing & Sales, Wine Sales and Distribution, and Artisan Public Relations, have won numerous international awards. He has recorded a series of lectures for the Great Courses called “The Instant Sommelier,” and a series of lectures on wine for Audible: “The Story of Wine in Ten Glasses.” He currently serves as Senior Advisor, Wine Tourism for the Expedia Wine Club Cruises and writes mystery novels set in California. His first series of mysteries is set in the Sierra Nevada and features wilderness ranger Dan Courtwright. A new book, A Murderous Vintage, featuring journalist Alex Stone, is set in the even more mysterious Napa Valley.

title: Feminist Book Club: Shut Up, This Is Serious by Carolina Ixta
description: Join us for an online discussion! The Feminist Book Club meets monthly to discuss books exploring feminist issues. Selections for the club span literature, memoir, graphic novels, essay collections and works of nonfiction. Hosted by Jenna Sanders and Stephanie Der, the Feminist Book Club is open to people and their experiences from multiple genders and races. Register to receive a link to the event one week prior. ABOUT THE BOOK WINNER OF THE PURA BELPRÉ YA AUTHOR AWARD \* A Morris Award Finalist \* Parade Best Young Adult Books of All Time \* Indie Next List Pick \* An unforgettable YA debut about two Latina teens growing up in East Oakland as they discover that the world is brimming with messy complexities, perfect for fans of Elizabeth Acevedo and Erika L. Sánchez. Belén Dolores Itzel del Toro wants the normal stuff: to experience love or maybe have a boyfriend or at least just lose her virginity. But nothing is normal in East Oakland. Her father left her family. She’s at risk of not graduating. And Leti, her super-Catholic, nerdy-ass best friend, is pregnant—by the boyfriend she hasn’t told her parents about, because he’s Black, and her parents are racist. Things are hella complicated. Weighed by a depression she can’t seem to shake, Belén helps Leti, hangs out with an older guy, and cuts a lot of class. She soon realizes, though, that distractions are only temporary. Leti is becoming a mother. Classmates are getting ready for college. But what about Belén? What future is there for girls like her? From debut author Carolina Ixta comes a fierce, intimate examination of friendship, chosen family, and the generational cycles we must break to become our truest selves. ABOUT THE AUTHOR Carolina Ixta is a writer from Oakland, California. A daughter of Mexican immigrants, she received her BA in creative writing and Spanish language and literature at the University of California, Santa Cruz, and obtained her master's degree in education at the University of California, Berkeley. Her debut novel, Shut Up, This Is Serious, was a Morris Award finalist, an LA Times Book Prize finalist, and the winner of the Pura Belpré Award. Few Blue Skies is her sophomore novel.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove. 

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

“Scott Ray Laws is an unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May ..and I HAD to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” Luigi- Owner-The Listening Room.

“..An ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song” -  Scotty O’Neill - Guitarist/Promoter

“ It was such a treat catching your set last night — really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us — we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.”  -Tripp B. - Sonoma Songwriter

“Expect slow burning passion and vivid music …the kind of energy that turns into “let’s stay for just one more!..”  - Doug- Owner/Wine Maker- Spicy Vines

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life...”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

DATE AND TIME: Thursdays, 5:30 PM

Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. Designed to be both a cardiovascular challenge and a deep toning session, this class focuses on the “powerhouse” of the body—your core.

By layering fluid, isolative movements over an athletic aerobic base, you will challenge your muscles in ways traditional gym workouts can’t reach.

What to Expect in Belly Dancing Class

• Core-Centric Power: Use undulations and shimmies to engage deep abdominal muscles for a tighter, stronger midsection.

• Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

“Whether you’re looking to define your waistline or simply want a workout that feels like a celebration, this class offers the perfect balance of sweat and grace.”

Difficulty Level: All levels welcome! No prior dance experience is required—just bring your energy and a willingness to move.

description:
Your First Steps into Bachata

This class is perfect for bachata beginners that want to learn basic steps and skills, or those who want to refresh their foundational skills. We understand that learning something new can feel a little intimidating. That’s why our supportive and relaxed environment is specifically designed to make learning bachata basics an absolute blast!

Our friendly instructors will guide you through:

**Basic directional steps:** You’ll learn the fundamental movements that form the building blocks of all bachata dancing.

**Proper frame for partner work:** Discover how to connect comfortably and effectively with a partner, setting you up for smooth and enjoyable dances.

**Simple turn patterns:** We’ll introduce you to easy-to-follow turn patterns that will have you dancing with a partner in no time.

We’ve carefully organized our curriculum to ensure that each movement is easy to grasp and remember, building your confidence with every step. Our goal is to make learning fun. Join us to learn Bachata in Marin.

Important Details

**No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Come join us and discover the joy of bachata! We can’t wait to see you on the dance floor.

title: Samba no Pé
description:
Get ready to feel the rhythm and energy of Rio de Janeiro! **Samba no Pé** (Samba in the Foot) is the captivating solo style of samba danced in the streets and at Carnival, known for its rapid, intricate footwork and infectious hip movements.

**You will learn**

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.

Rhythm & Musicality: You will learn how to connect your movement directly to the irresistible beat of the bateria (the samba drum section).

This class is perfect for anyone looking to connect with the vibrant spirit of Brazil, improve coordination, and get a fantastic workout—all while learning the foundational steps of this iconic dance. No partner or prior dance experience is required! Just bring your enthusiasm and comfortable shoes!

Date & Time: Thursdays @6:30PM – 7:30PM

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway #8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

title: Uncovering Sonoma Terroir: What's Really in Your Vineyard Soil? 🍇
description:
Have you wondered why Pinot lovers talk about Goldridge soil? Or maybe you’ve been trying to figure out why some areas of your vineyard just don’t seem to produce as well as others. The answer might be right under your feet! Come to our November 12 meeting to learn more about the soils of Sonoma and the criticality of matching rootstock, variety and soil to get the best out of your vineyard.

Dr. Paul Anamosa will discuss these intricacies on November 12th at the Sonoma Community Center during a presentation hosted by Sonoma Home Winemakers. Titled *"It’s Soil, not Dirt! – The Importance of Soil Analysis in Making Better Wine,"* the session details the soils of Sonoma County and highlights how understanding soil composition, structure, and chemistry helps winemakers and enthusiasts make smarter decisions from vine to glass.

📍 Sonoma Community Center, Room 110, 276 E. Napa St. Sonoma

⏰ Doors open at 6:30 p.m. | Presentation at 7:00 p.m.

🍷 Free and open to the public (21+ for wine tasting; please bring your own glass and winemakers, a bottle to share for the evening).

description:
Greg Lamboy has called Finnegan's Marin home for over a decade. Every second Thursday of the month, this Tiburon-based troubadour settles into the warmly lit corner of Novato's beloved neighborhood pub and does what he does best: connects. An accomplished guitarist and award-winning songwriter, Lamboy has earned his stripes across the Bay Area scene both as a solo artist and as frontman of Pacific Standard, his soulful Americana band. His five acclaimed albums draw praise for melodies that are pitch-perfect and lyrics that feel like they were written specifically for you. title: River Shook
description:
River Shook releases their galvanizing self-titled solo debut on June 26.

With arrow-to-the-heart honesty, vivid characters, soaring electric guitar, and shimmering pedal steel, Shook's unmistakable voice cuts through darkness like a beam of light. The album carries a sense of poise and strength, urging listeners toward deeper self-reflection and honesty about their lives and choices.

In spring 2025, as Sarah Shook & the Disarmers neared the end of their decade-long run, Shook was already envisioning a new chapter and writing for their solo debut album. When a strong batch of demos yielded no bites from labels, Shook pitched an unconventional idea to their lead guitarist and partner, Blake Tallent: they would co-produce the record on a shoestring budget. After the final Disarmers’ show in June, the pair immediately began recording in their home studio, driven by a renewed passion and a shared creative vision.

The result is a bold leap forward in production. Shook describes the process as more than evolution. "I had to completely kill my old self," they explain, shedding limiting beliefs to fully realize the record’s full potential. Tallent proves a crucial collaborator, playing nearly every instrument on the record and helping shape a sound that feels expansive despite its minimal resources. Together, free from outside influence or contractual pressure, the pair created something deeply personal and sonically singular.

Across the album, Shook explores love, distance, freedom, and self-revelation. From the wistful urgency of "Country Angel" to the road-worn vulnerability of "If We Got A Chance" and the cinematic longing of "Lost Without Your Love," the songs balance heartbreak with defiance. Recorded in a rural North Carolina home studio, River Shook feels larger than life–an intimate yet sweeping work that confronts hard truths while reminding listeners of their capacity to change.

title: Gain Speaking Confidence with Mare Island Toastmasters
description:
We meet in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month. However, you can catch us online every Thursday unless the meeting date falls on a holiday.

Please register at https://signup.com/go/WiniixA

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

Toastmasters International is all about communication excellence, and for 100 years and counting, Toastmasters have been expressing themselves better, practicing, and evaluating in a fun club environment, shining all around the world.

https://mareisland.toastmastersclubs.org/

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: California Native Creations Art Show

description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.
